# European Commission Publications on General-Purpose AI Obligations (as of September 2026)

By September 2026, the European Commission's key publications addressing GPAI obligations under the AI Act included:

## Guidelines on the Scope of Obligations

The Commission issued formal **Guidelines on the scope of obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models under the AI Act**, clarifying which providers fall within scope and what they must do. The guidelines clarify that GPAI obligations entered into application on 2 August 2025, with Article 50 transparency duties applying from 2 August 2026 and Articles 53–56 GPAI obligations actively enforceable [1][2].

The guidelines cover core requirements including:
- Provision of technical documentation to authorities and downstream providers
- Compliance with EU copyright law
- Publication of summaries of training data content
- The principle that only significant model modifications trigger provider obligations
- Special rules for free/open-source GPAI providers (limited mainly to copyright and training-summary duties) and additional obligations (evaluations, adversarial testing, incident reporting, cybersecurity) for models presenting systemic risk (e.g., trained above 10^25 FLOPs) [2][3].

The guidelines are downloadable in all 24 EU official languages, accompanied by a **Communication approving the content of the guidelines** (in English) [4].

## General-Purpose AI Code of Practice

The Commission and the AI Board confirmed that the **General-Purpose AI Code of Practice** is an **adequate voluntary tool** for providers of GPAI models to demonstrate compliance with the AI Act. The Code focuses on Articles 53 and 55 regarding transparency requirements [5][6]. The Code of Practice is **in force as of 9 September 2026** [7].

## Related Press Releases and Communications

- **31 July 2026 press release**: Announced the Commission would begin enforcing AI Act rules and new transparency requirements starting 2 August 2026 [8].
- **1 September 2026**: The Commission confirmed it had written to more than a certain number of providers regarding compliance with the AI Act [9].
- **29 September 2026 press release**: Appeared on the Commission's AI policy page but concerned copyright rather than GPAI obligations specifically [8].

## Status as of 15 September 2026

As of mid-September 2026, the EU AI Act was in its active 2026 enforcement phase, with Article 50 transparency duties applicable from 2 August 2026, new prohibited-practice dates landing on 2 December 2026, and Annex III high-risk system obligations using 2 December 2027 as the key date [2].
